statement: The first line holds n; the next n lines each hold one word. Print the longest word such that every one of its prefixes - length 1, 2, and so on up to the word itself - is also present in the list. When several longest candidates tie, print the lexicographically smallest; when no word qualifies, print none. Build a trie with end-of-word flags, then check candidates: a word qualifies when every node along its path carries the flag.
constraints: Words are lowercase, length 1 to 20, all distinct.

example.input:
6
n
ni
nin
ninj
ninja
ninga
example.why: Each prefix of ninja is in the list; ninga fails because ning is missing.

hint: Walk each word through the trie and demand the end flag at every single step.
mistake: Checking only that the word itself is stored - the chain of flagged prefixes is the actual condition.
